note: The browser WITH its sandbox, run by a normal user, as on any Linux that allows user namespaces. On the Ubuntu 24.04 runner AppArmor refuses them to a user, so every other non-root suite runs a browser WITHOUT the sandbox of its socket and content processes; the gate turns the restriction off for this leg (sysctl kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=0) and the first test fails unless the socket and a tab process have a seccomp filter (Seccomp: 2). The three situations of the UDP line: A (a proxy that carries UDP: the srflx born through the relay), B (no proxy: the gather is real), C (a proxy with no UDP: the ICE server name goes by DoH through the proxy and the gather ends in 701). No root and no resolver trap needed.
linux_only: It reads the seccomp filter of the socket and tab processes in /proc. The Windows twin reads the sandbox token of the same processes (integrity level, restrictions) and needs a measurement of the retail Firefox's tokens first; until then Linux only.

Linux needs root: the resolver trap of the file (ResolverTrap) points /etc/resolv.conf at a counting resolver on port 53. Su Windows il resolver trap non gira: l'asserzione sul resolver di sistema è l'unica omessa. Run it without xdist (port 53 is one per host). On the Linux leg the gate exports INVPW_REQUIRE_TRAP=1: a trap that cannot run or bind port 53 is a failure, not a skipped assertion.
